stories.headline: Big Study Tracks Health
stories.summary: Australia has launched an 18 and Up study to follow 100,000 people over their lives to better understand mental illness and early-onset cancer.
key_points: 100,000 people will be recruited for Australia’s largest intergenerational study of wellbeing and ageing.
The study will follow people aged 18 to 90+ throughout their lives.
Almost two in five Australians aged 16 to 24 experienced a mental disorder in the past year.
Participants’ data may be linked to cancer registries and Medicare with consent.
stories.why_it_matters: Long-term evidence could help improve prevention, treatments and care systems for younger generations.

stories.headline: Healthwatch Gets Reprieve
stories.summary: Yvette Cooper has dropped plans to abolish Healthwatch England after a backlash from MPs, keeping the patient voice in the NHS.
key_points: Healthwatch England and its 150 branches will continue.
The body collects and analyses patient feedback on NHS services.
MPs from Labour, Conservative and Liberal Democrat parties had criticised the planned abolition.
Healthwatch has reported problems such as dental access and years-long ADHD waits.
stories.why_it_matters: Keeping an independent patient champion helps surface problems in care and supports better NHS accountability.

stories.headline: More GP Care Covered
stories.summary: More Australians are being bulk-billed for GP care after new federal incentives for doctors and practices.
key_points: 63% of Australians are now bulk-billed for all their GP care, up from 56%.
26% of GPs reported bulk-billing all of their patients, up from 12%.
The share delaying GP care due to cost fell from 8.8% to 7.7%.
stories.why_it_matters: Lower costs make primary care easier to access, which can help more people get timely treatment and support.
